clue.text: Secluded regular

definitions.meaning: secluded means hidden away, out of public view
a regular is an ordinary soldier of the lowest rank in a standing army

explanation.surface: A soldier who keeps to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Something secluded is personal and kept apart, and a regular soldier of the lowest rank is a so-called ordinary ranker.

clue.text: Hickory tree snares long island bird

indicators.note: snares means traps, holding the other letters inside

parts.note: the pecan is a kind of hickory tree

explanation.surface: A tree catching a bird from a long island.
explanation.definitionFit: The large waterbird with a throat pouch is a seabird.

clue.text: Genuine kind of naïve young woman

indicators.note: kind of hints at a version of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An innocent girl of a sincere sort.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an artless, innocent girl, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: At an easy pace speculator is topped and tailed

indicators.note: topping and tailing removes the head and end, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: a gambler speculates on outcomes

explanation.surface: A slow-moving investor gets his head and feet cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as walking at an easy pace, a verb sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To stroll or walk leisurely is to move at a relaxed speed.

clue.text: Someone who improves things, mentored a change

indicators.note: change signals the letters of mentored a being rearranged

explanation.surface: A coach who altered something to improve it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emendator corrects texts, making improvements.

clue.text: Is page "s" about dolphins?

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a dictionary page under S covers dolphins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges IS and PAGE into SEAPIG; the quoted S is then added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea pigs is an old name for porpoises and dolphins, marine mammals likened to swine.

clue.text: What I was on when I met a man who wasn't there

definitions.text: What I was on when I met a man who wasn't there

parts.words: What I was on when I met a man who wasn't there
parts.note: quotes the poem Antigonish: 'Yesterday, upon the ...', where the speaker met a man who wasn't there

explanation.surface: Recalling a well-known nonsense poem about an absent man.
explanation.definitionFit: In the poem the speaker meets the absent man on a step.

clue.text: New religion encompassed by starry involvement with forefathers

indicators.note: encompassed by means surrounded by, so the new religion goes inside

parts.note: astral means relating to the stars
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A new faith wrapped up in stargazing and ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestral means relating to or inherited from one's forebears.

clue.text: Russian, without capital, of an European area

indicators.note: without capital means losing the first letter

parts.note: a Siberian comes from part of Russia

explanation.surface: A Russian minus the capital city in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian means of the peninsula containing Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Church spire the French find expensive at first

indicators.note: at first places this piece before the other

parts.note: steep means excessively expensive
le is French for the

explanation.surface: The French find a church tower costly to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped by a pointed structure.

clue.text: Indiscriminate libel, eg is easy to read

indicators.note: indiscriminate suggests letters thrown together at random, so libel and eg are jumbled

explanation.surface: A careless libel, for example, is at least plain to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Handwriting that is clear enough to make out is called legible.

clue.text: Unite a number on the island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: Bringing together a group of people living on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow together or fuse into one mass.

clue.text: Criminal's offer to become a sporty opponent

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
a tender is a formal offer

explanation.surface: A crook's bid to turn into a sporting rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival competing for a title or prize in sport.

clue.text: Scanty commoner chases a runner

indicators.note: something that chases another comes after it, so this piece follows

parts.note: a ski is a runner on which one slides over snow
an MP sits in the House of Commons, so is a commoner

explanation.surface: A poor, ordinary person pursuing an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: MP = Member of Parliament, who sits in the Commons.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, skimp is an old word for meagre or barely sufficient.

clue.text: Relative could be pleasant up to a point

indicators.note: taking in the point, the word for pleasant is filled up with it inside

parts.note: nice means pleasant
E is east, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A family member who is agreeable, but only within limits.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family relation.

clue.text: Like ivory but use bone carved with ruthenium

indicators.note: carved means cut and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Ru is the chemical symbol for ruthenium

explanation.surface: Ivory-like carving made from bone and a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Eburneous means resembling ivory, from Latin ebur.

clue.text: Ability to endure patience

definitions.meaning: the capacity to withstand something such as a drug or hardship
forbearance with others' views or behaviour

explanation.surface: Defining endurance as simply being patient.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both physical capacity to withstand and the forbearance of putting up with others.

clue.text: Ghastly action started lately underwater clear of the headland

indicators.note: started means the starts of the words lately underwater are taken

parts.note: rid of means clear of
ness is a headland

explanation.surface: A ghastly deed done underwater off a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Luridness is the quality of being gruesome or sensational.

clue.text: Queer carl became a varnisher

indicators.note: became signals that the letters change into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: An odd fellow took up a trade finishing furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: A carl is an old word for a churl or peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who coats wood or metal with lacquer is a varnisher.

clue.text: All in on manufacture of ointment base

indicators.note: manufacture of hints at the letters being made into something new

explanation.surface: Everyone working on making an ointment base.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin, wool fat, is used as a base for ointments.

clue.text: Adapt to study behaviour

parts.note: to con is to study
form is good behaviour, as in bad form

explanation.surface: Advice to observe and adjust one's conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to fit in with rules or norms.

clue.text: Out-of-office king is more tardy

parts.note: late can mean former, no longer holding office, as in the late chairman
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch who has stepped down is now even slower.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more delayed or behind time comes afterwards.

clue.text: Pub next to a guesthouse

parts.note: a tavern is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub beside a guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A taverna is a Greek inn or restaurant.

clue.text: Mitigate release

definitions.meaning: to free someone from duty or a burden

explanation.surface: Ease off and let go.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to ease suffering and to free from a duty or post.

clue.text: Ulster — not French — fabric

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster
non is French for not

explanation.surface: Cloth from Northern Ireland, not from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a light, sheer silk or voile cloth.

clue.text: Made a live broadcast of the middle ages

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Televising a period drama as it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval describes the period roughly from the fifth to the fifteenth century.

clue.text: Pals arise, determined, before noon

indicators.note: in a down clue arise means rising up, so the pieces read upwards

parts.note: set means determined
AM is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: Friends get up early, resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: Mates are friends.

clue.text: Weald earthwork reveals a Spanish Hamlet

indicators.note: reveals means letters are shown inside the words Weald earthwork

explanation.surface: An excavation in an English region uncovers a Spanish village.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a wooded region of south-east England; Hamlet is capitalised to suggest Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldea is Spanish for a village.

clue.text: Beware! There's a sentry about

definitions.meaning: a warning cry to be careful
a guard posted to keep watch

explanation.surface: A warning that a guard is near.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a shouted warning to watch out and a person keeping watch.

clue.text: Close alternative points to sign

parts.note: the close of something is its end
or introduces an alternative
S and E are south and east, compass points

explanation.surface: A nearby option points the way to a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one's signature on the back of a cheque or document, or to back publicly.

clue.text: Greek goddess is an unbeatable rival

definitions.meaning: an opponent one can never overcome

explanation.surface: A deity who is always the winner.
explanation.definitionFit: The goddess of retribution gave her name to anyone's long-standing undefeatable foe.

clue.text: Tory in a furious state over toll

indicators.note: in places the Tory abbreviation inside the word for a furious state

parts.note: savage means fierce or furious
C stands for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: A Conservative in a rage about a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Scavage was an old duty levied on goods sold by outside merchants in a town.
